desc:
Let m be the length of the string p. For every substring of s of length m, ask: what is the smallest number of characters that must be replaced (each replaced by any letter) so that the substring becomes an anagram of p?

Count the substrings (by start position) for which this smallest number is at most k.

s = "cbaxyz", p = "abc", k = 1
cba -> 0 replacements
bax -> 1 (x becomes c)
axy -> 2
xyz -> 3
result = 2
constraints: s and p consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Think about which characters of a window are already 'in the right place' in the multiset sense. The rest must be replaced.
The number of characters of a window that can be kept is the sum over letters of min(window count, need count). The replacements needed equal m minus that sum.

Maintain that sum while sliding: when a letter enters and its window count is still below its need, the sum grows by one; when a letter leaves and its count was at most its need, the sum shrinks by one.
editorial: For one window, the characters that can stay are matched against p letter by letter: for each letter c we can keep at most min(have[c], need[c]) copies. All remaining positions must be replaced, and replacement is always enough, since the leftover positions can take exactly the letters that p still lacks. So the cost is m - sum_c min(have[c], need[c]).

Keep the array have for the current window and the running value matched = sum_c min(have[c], need[c]). Adding a letter c: if have[c] < need[c] before the addition, matched increases by one. Removing a letter c: after decrementing, if have[c] < need[c], matched decreases by one. A window counts when m - matched <= k. Total time O(n + m), space O(1).
